name: apple-notes-mcp
description: Read, search and write Apple Notes through the Notes app
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Notes app on this Mac.

Notes has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Notes.app itself through Apple events. Notes must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

Every result is bounded. Lists of accounts, folders, notes and attachments come one page at a time, and a note comes as its first 10000 characters; each result says in its first lines what it left out and what to pass for the rest. A search looks at no more than 500 notes and for no longer than 45 seconds, and says so when it stops early. A call that has not finished after 120 seconds is answered with an error.

Notes are returned as plain text by default rather than HTML: it is what you actually want to read, and it costs a fraction of the tokens.

update_note makes you say whether you are appending or replacing. Silently replacing a long note is the mistake worth designing against.

Tags and pinning are not here. Notes' scripting dictionary does not expose them at all — they need the Shortcuts server instead.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: notes_status
tools.description: Reports whether Notes is running, whether this server may automate it, and what limits are in force. Reads no notes.

tools.name: notes_accounts
tools.description: Lists the Notes accounts — iCloud, On My Mac, an Exchange account — 50 to a page in name order, with how many folders each holds. Pass limit and offset for more.

tools.name: notes_folders
tools.description: Lists the folders, 100 to a page ordered by account, then path, each with its note count and the path to address it by. Nested folders appear as 'Parent/Child'. Pass limit and offset for more.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.description: Finds notes by text, folder, account and date (from_date, to_date) and returns 25 to a page, the most recently modified first: one line per note with its id, never the note's contents. Pass limit and offset for more; follow it with note_get.

tools.name: note_get
tools.description: Returns one note: its folder, dates and attachment count, then the first 10000 characters of its text, as plain text. Pass character_offset and max_characters to read a longer note one window at a time.

tools.name: note_attachments
tools.description: Lists what is attached to one note, 20 to a page, the first added first: name, dates, the link a URL attachment points at, and the cid: reference it appears under in the note's HTML. Pass limit and offset for more.

tools.name: create_note
tools.description: Adds a new note to a folder. The note's title is the first line of the body, because that is how Notes works — there is no separate title.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Changes a note's content. 'mode' is REQUIRED: append adds to the end, replace discards the whole note and writes the new text instead.

tools.name: move_note
tools.description: Moves a note into a different folder. Its content is untouched.

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Deletes a note. Requires confirm=true, and returns the record it removed with the first 10000 characters of its text, so what was lost is at least written down somewhere.
